subject: Post-discovery: Hyperscaler perf delta, test cadence & procurement asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@acme.com>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: Hyperscaler perf delta, test cadence & procurement asks

Thanks for the time today — appreciated the candid read on expected latency SLOs and procurement timing. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard
- Acme is targeting a p95 <= 120ms for 256-token prompts in production for the search assistant workload.
- Current hyperscaler-managed endpoints hit ~130–180ms p95 depending on routing and instance type; p99 spikes are the real blocker during concurrency bursts.
- Procurement is on a 60-day cadence; technical evaluation must be complete before legal/finance loop.

Preliminary findings (from our quick lab sweep)
- Redwood-hosted (v2) with continuous batching and prefix KV cache: p95 ~110ms, p99 ~200ms at 50 concurrent sessions on n1-standard gpus (quantized 4-bit profile).
- Hyperscaler baseline (public endpoint) showed p95 ~140ms, p99 ~320ms under same synthetic load — consistent with what Kenji outlined.
- Tokens/sec (steady-state generation) for our tuned path: ~720 tokens/sec across the pool; hyperscaler endpoint measured ~480 tokens/sec in our sweep.

Proposed next tests (A/B focused) — immediate items
1) Controlled A/B run vs hyperscaler public endpoint (same model family, same tokenization) — measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec for: short (64), medium (256), long (1024) prompts.
2) Stress bursts to capture p99 under transient concurrency (10s and 60s bursts).
3) Variant test: Redwood quantized path vs hyperscaler float32 and 8-bit quantized offering (if available).
4) Cold-start latency profiling (first-token latency for new sessions, warmed vs cold KV cache).

Operational asks from Acme to unblock procurement
- Can Acme provide a representative prompt set (5–10 prompts) and a daytime concurrency window to replay? (helps keep the tests realistic)
- Will Acme allow us a short sandbox account with limited data retention for two weeks?

Deliverables & timing
- We’ll run the A/B sweep and share a summarized CSV and a one-pager SLO gap analysis within 5 business days after receiving the prompt set.
- Follow-up call to review results and procurement asks: propose 2028-07-19 or 2028-07-20.

Attachments: quick lab CSV (acme-hyperscaler-ab-results.csv) and the internal test plan (redwood-ab-test-plan.md).

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Hyperscaler perf delta, test cadence & procurement asks

Thanks Marcus — solid recap. A few clarifications before we hand over the prompt set: 

1) Concurrency: our typical peak daytime window is 08:00–10:00 PT, ~120 concurrent real users (but these are short chat-like interactions; many will be <200 tokens). For the test, let's do a scaled-down 50 concurrency run first, then a 120 concurrency stress run.
2) Model parity: we can share model names; the hyperscaler is running their custom-tuned 7B variant. Can you confirm you’ll mirror the same model family and tokenizer?
3) Sandbox: procurement will provision a sandbox with IP allowlist; retention policy must be 7 days. Is that acceptable?

One more ask: can you include a breakdown in the deliverable showing cost per 1M tokens for both configurations (your tuned path vs hyperscaler)? That will help our finance team during the procurement window.

-Elliot

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-13T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Hyperscaler perf delta, test cadence & procurement asks

Appreciate the quick reply, Elliot. Short answers inline and next actions below.

- Concurrency plan: yes — we’ll run a two-stage sweep: 50 concurrent steady-state then the 120-concurrency 5-minute burst. That will expose p99 amplification.
- Model parity: we can mirror the same model family and tokenizer. If the hyperscaler has a custom-tuned checkpoint, we’ll match architecture + tokenization and run the same prompt set to be fair. Please share model identifier.
- Sandbox & retention: 7-day retention is fine; we’ll wipe logs after the window and provide an audit entry.
- Cost breakdown: Karthik will produce a simple cost-per-1M-tokens table (redwood hosted path vs hyperscaler) — expect that with the CSV results.

Internal notes / runbook (high level)
- Test harness: use the same request pacing, deterministic RNG seeds, and synthetic user think-times. Capture per-request: first-token latency, last-token latency, tokens/sec, cpu/gpu utilization, and queue depth.
- Configs to exercise: (A) Redwood tuned path (batching + cache + 4-bit quantization), (B) Hyperscaler public endpoint default, (C) Hyperscaler if available with 8-bit quantization.
- Acceptance criteria to highlight to Acme: p95 <=120ms AND p99 <=300ms in steady-state; cold-start first-token <= 250ms for new sessions.

Next actions / owners
- Acme: share prompt set, model id, and sandbox IP allowlist (Elliot).
- Redwood: we (marcus_lin, marissa_cole) will schedule the runs once sandbox credentials are live; Karthik produces cost sheet; Jordan will prepare a one-page SLO gap figure for the review call.

Proposed review call: 2028-07-19 10:00 PT — Marcus to set invite after sandbox is provisioned.

Attachments: test plan and quick-sweep CSV attached.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
Date: 2028-07-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Hyperscaler perf delta, test cadence & procurement asks

Got it — sharing prompt set and model id by EOD today, and procurement will spin up the sandbox with the 7-day retention + IP allowlist (Kenji at the hyperscaler is copied on provisioning). 2028-07-19 10:00 PT works for the review.

Appreciate the clear acceptance criteria — looking forward to the gap analysis.

Best,
Elliot
